title: Inference Flow Signal Mapper — Visual guidance for batching & cache tradeoffs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Teams deploying Redwood need fast, trustworthy guidance for batching and prefix/KV cache settings. Existing UI surfaces either present raw knobs (hard to reason about) or opaque recommendations without clear signal mapping. Goal: design an interactive 'Signal Mapper' canvas in the Console that shows how observable request signals (avg sequence length, prefix hit rate, streaming vs non-streaming, QPS, user-level reuse) map to recommended batching and cache configurations, and simulate expected cost/latency trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive canvas that maps 4 primary signals to recommended presets with rationale cards
Simulation panel shows p50/p95 latency and per-token cost delta for selected preset across a synthetic 1-hour workload
Guardrail warnings appear when a recommended preset may increase risk to user-facing quality (e.g., aggressive quantization + high temperature)
One-click apply persists config to a selected route and creates a canary rollout (10% by default)
Design accessible: keyboard operable, color contrast >= 4.5:1, and screen-reader descriptions for each control
Prototype validated in 5 moderated usability sessions with engineers and platform owners and feedback loop captured
comments: 2026-02-20 - Asha Patel: Drafted initial concept after two ops interviews. Proposed mapping signals: avg_seq_len, prefix_reuse_rate, qps_burstiness, streaming_fraction. Added sketches for slider + radar view.

2026-02-24 - Marco Reyes: Reviewed sketch. Ask: include a simple cost delta estimate and show conservative vs aggressive presets. Flag: need backend metric availability for prefix_reuse_rate (ENG to confirm).

2026-02-26 - Priya Menon (ENG): Confirmed we can surface prefix_reuse_rate and qps_burstiness from the metrics pipeline but at 60s granularity. Noted simulation must accept aggregated input rather than per-request traces.

2026-03-01 - Design critique (Lina Zhou, Tomás Alvarez): Suggested replace radar visualization with stacked contribution bars to improve readability for non-ML PMs. Requested stronger microcopy to explain guardrail triggers.

2026-03-05 - Usability testing: 5 participants (SREs and ML platform engineers). Key findings: users liked the visual mapping and rationale cards; confused by the ambiguity of 'aggressive' label — renamed to 'performance-first'. Users asked for an explicit fallback action to revert when quality alerts fire.

2026-03-08 - Marco Reyes: Iterated prototype to include a revert button and canary rollout modal. Added inline cost per 1M tokens estimate. TODO: add e2e tests and telemetry events to measure adoption.
2026-03-10 - Product review (Evelyn Grant): Approved concept. Asked PM to prioritize integration with Rollouts feature and to expose preview of how changes affect the Dashboard cost view.

2026-03-12 - Engineering review (Ethan Brooks): Flagged performance concern for simulation; recommended running a lightweight server-side simulation job rather than client-only compute for large models. Agreed to add a throttle and a cached results layer.
accessibility_considerations: Canvas elements must be keyboard reachable. Provide descriptive aria-labels for each slider and rationale card. Ensure color choices meet contrast guidelines; provide texture pattern alternatives for color-blind users.
usability_findings: Participants preferred explicit numeric estimates over vague descriptors (e.g., show +$0.06/1k tokens)
Ambiguous labels (aggressive/conservative) caused hesitation; renaming to 'performance-first' and 'cost-first' improved clarity
Users expect an immediate preview of Dashboard cost impact before applying presets
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-offs: exposing too many knobs increases cognitive load — we prioritize 3 presets (cost-first, balanced, performance-first) with an advanced panel for power users. Simulation accuracy vs responsiveness: server-run simulations more accurate but add latency; compromise by returning a fast client-side first-pass plus an async server estimate that updates the UI. Rollout integration: default canary 10% with automatic rollback trigger if quality regressions exceed configured thresholds.
